name: Strand Memorial
description: A civic memorial to the founder of Meridian: one hundred square metres, a docent, and an allocation that renews without review. What it actually is changes depending on who is standing in front of it and what you did three centuries upstream.

variants.description: Not a memorial any more. People have been bringing things: handwriting, wire flowers, a prayer wheel, a child's drawing of a machine with a face on it. The allocation office stopped removing them at some point and did not announce that it had.
The monument is down and the archive behind it is dark. Nobody has been allocated to clear the site, and allocation is how this century says what a thing is worth.

A museum, and a careful one: founding documents behind glass, a timeline with no visible gaps in it, and a plaque naming Callum Strand a steward of the public interest. The nineteen months the 2148 curator could not fill are not marked here at all.
